final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest phenotype escape z-score (0.665) among evaluated candidates. Loss of this V3-loop-proximal N-glycan is a known antibody-escape mechanism with generally preserved replication.
Strong escape evidence (z=0.638) from an inner-domain glycan-deletion event. Removing the N384 glycan shifts the glycan shield while typically retaining fitness.
Moderate escape signal (z=0.558) at the V3 base glycan. Deletion of N301 is a well-tolerated escape route for several V3-directed antibodies.

stop_reason.detail: Max tool calls and rounds consumed; final Top-3 fixed from accumulated phenotype evidence and domain knowledge.

history.rationale: Disrupts an N-linked glycan motif near the V3 base (PNN at 299–301), a common route to escape glycan-dependent V3 bnAbs while retaining core Env folding.

N301 lies in the V3 loop base; loss of this N-glycan is a known escape route for V3-glycan-targeting bNAbs while V3 base mutations are often replication-tolerant. Retained pending EVEscape and ESM-1v evidence.
Lowest escape score of the three (0.558) and N301 glycan loss has known folding/processing costs; still a classic PGT128/10-1074 escape node, so retain but downrank.
Decent escape signal (z=0.558) at a V3 glycan; retained pending fitness-plausibility evidence.
Moderate escape z=0.558; N301 is a V3-loop N-glycan whose removal is escape-relevant but has slightly higher fitness cost uncertainty than N279/N384, keeping it rank 3.
Glycan site at the CD4bs-proximal loop (278–279 NN) whose removal can reduce neutralization by CD4bs/glycan-dependent antibodies with limited folding impact.
N279 anchors the 276-glycan hole in BG505 relevant to 10-1074/3BNC117-class N332/V3-glycan supersite escape. Moderate prior; needs phenotype and plausibility evidence.
Highest EVEscape score (0.665) among tested candidates; V3-loop-adjacent glycan loss with moderate fitness cost expected. Retain as current leader but fitness-proxiom evidence still needed.
Highest EVEscape z-score (0.665) among evaluated candidates at a V3-proximal glycan site; glycan loss here is a classic escape mechanism with moderate fitness cost.
Highest EVEscape z-score (0.665) among all measured candidates; N279 glycan loss in the C2/V3 region is a tolerated, fitness-compatible escape mechanism in BG505-like Envs.
Loss of the V4-loop glycan at position 384, a variable, well-tolerated surface patch where glycan shifts confer escape.
N384 is near the N386 position but a less-established escape site; down-ranked in favor of N386A. Retained only pending evidence.
Strong escape score (0.638); N384 is a V1V2-region glycan where loss is often tolerated in tier-2 Envs. Needs plausibility check before finalizing.
Strong escape signal (z=0.638) at a glycan hole-adjacent site; needs a plausibility check since glycan deletions can reduce fitness.
Strong escape signal (z=0.638) with a small upward adjustment given it removes a glycan adjacent to the V3 glycan canopy without abolishing known folding-critical disulfides.
Glycan at the V3-stem/C3 region (position 337 N); deletion can affect quaternary-antibody recognition with plausible fitness retention.
N337 is a clade-conserved glycan near the V3 base whose loss often impairs folding and is not a major escape node; deprioritized in favor of N332A.

rejection.reason: N337 is a clade-conserved glycan near the V3 base whose loss often impairs folding and is not a major escape node; deprioritized in favor of N332A.

history.rationale: Contact-site mutation in the CD4bs-adjacent loop that can reduce CD4bs-antibody sensitivity, but carries higher replication-fitness risk.
D366 in the CD4bs rarely mediates high-escape while CD4 contact changes risk entry fitness; weak prior with no supporting evidence.
